A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the compounds containing 1,2- or 1,3-diazine nucleus and 1,3,4-oxadiazole ring were found to possess moderate antimicrobial activity against test microorganisms.

we were able to synthesize new derivatives of 7-amino-3-cephem-4-carboxylic acid and 3-carboxy-7-oxo-4-thia-1-azabicyclo[3.2.0]heptane-2-carboxylic acids containing different heteroaromatic nuclei and sulfonylamino group in the cephalo-sporanic acid skeleton.

the compounds containing 7-[(1,3-thia-zol-2-yl)methylamino]-cephalosporinic acid nucleus and the 4-aminophenylsulfonamide function were found to possess the most potent antibacterial and antiurease activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 4-nitrosulfonylamino group is a good substituent in cephalosporin nucleus.
the 7-amino group in the cephalospornanic acid skeleton can be used for the synthesis of a number of biologically active compounds.
the 7-amino-3-cephem-4-carboxylic acid nucleus can serve as a scaffold for the synthesis of novel compounds with potential biological activities.
